options.text: A region where gravity is stronger than normal
A region where a magnetic force is experienced
A region where a charged particle experiences a force
A flow of electrons through a conductor

questions.explanation: An electric field is defined as a region of space where a charged particle experiences a force. Any object with electric charge creates an electric field around it.

questions.stem: In which direction do electric field lines point around an isolated positive charge?

options.text: Parallel to the surface of the charge

questions.explanation: Electric field lines point away from positive charges and towards negative charges. This follows the convention that field direction shows the force on a positive test charge.

questions.stem: What do closely spaced electric field lines indicate?
questions.explanation: The density of electric field lines represents the field strength. Closely spaced lines indicate a stronger electric field, while widely spaced lines indicate a weaker field.

questions.stem: What is the electric field strength defined as?

options.text: The force per unit charge (E = F/Q)

questions.explanation: Electric field strength is defined as the force per unit positive charge, given by E = F/Q. It is measured in newtons per coulomb (N/C).

questions.stem: Between two parallel charged plates, the electric field is:

options.text: Uniform with equally spaced parallel field lines

questions.explanation: Between two parallel charged plates, the electric field is uniform. The field lines are parallel, equally spaced, and perpendicular to the plates, giving the same field strength throughout.

questions.stem: Which formula correctly relates electric field strength to voltage between parallel plates?
questions.explanation: For a uniform field between parallel plates, the electric field strength equals the potential difference divided by the distance between the plates: E = V/d, measured in V/m.

questions.stem: A positive charge is placed in a uniform electric field. In which direction does it accelerate?

options.text: Opposite to the direction of the electric field
In the direction of the electric field

questions.explanation: A positive charge accelerates in the direction of the electric field, since the field direction is defined as the direction of force on a positive test charge. Negative charges would accelerate in the opposite direction.
